answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a stake that vests slowly, like water wearing down marble: a new identity starts with zero trust and earns it only through verified work over time. One operator spinning up thousands of clones faces a dune of cost, because each clone needs its own stake and its own history, so flooding the market turns from cheap to ruinous. Trust is shaded in umber rather than black and white: partial scores let honest newcomers trade small while capping the damage any fresh identity can do before it proves itself.
